summary: Integrate Web Worker-based v86 WebAssembly Alpine Linux VM
description: Implement a standalone Web Worker wrapper to boot a minimal WebAssembly Alpine Linux image. This offloads x86 instruction execution from the browser's UI thread.
acceptance_criteria: Worker compiles and boots Alpine in under 3 seconds
No dropped frames on main window dragging
Successfully pipes Serial Out streams

summary: Implement Transactional Sync and Auto-Save for JSONL.gz Storage
description: Create an auto-save loop in CompressedStorageEngine that tracks file state dirty bits. If a file is modified, perform a debounced transactional append into IndexedDB.
acceptance_criteria: Changes auto-saved after 500ms of user/app idle
IndexedDB transaction commits raw binary ArrayBuffer
Decompression retrieves 100% of data with zero corruption

summary: Establish Reverse Proxy Engine for Installing Third-Party CORS-Protected Plugins
description: Create a CORS bypass engine using a secure pre-configured proxy helper to pull external manifest files from non-CORS domains.
acceptance_criteria: Fetch metadata from external links
Apply strict input sanitization on manifest JSON attributes
Reject non-secure origins

summary: Implement Event Hook Interceptors and Multi-Agent Orchestrator
description: Design system-level hooks inside the OS kernel to allow a background Agent to listen to user operations and coordinate sub-agents using capability tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Global event bus exposes system triggers safely to Agent
Orchestrator Agent can securely request fs:write
Automatic compilation of reports in VFS without human intervention

summary: Implement KB-MCP Integration for Browser-Based AI Agent
description: Integrate Vortex OS with the centralized KB-MCP server to provide persistent long-term semantic, episodic, and procedural memory to the in-browser AI Agent. Implement secure Host-side capability token verification ('kb-mcp:read', 'kb-mcp:write') before forwarding REST requests to https://kb.yapweijun1996.com.
acceptance_criteria: Sandboxed plugin cannot access KB-MCP server without declaring 'kb-mcp:read' or 'kb-mcp:write' permissions
Host OS successfully routes valid, tokenized messages over the MessageChannel IPC
AI Agent successfully reads/writes vector items through the CORS-authorized Host proxy

summary: Resolve Terminal Iframe Direct Load and Missing Worker Assets
description: Resolve the blank screen/script execution error caused by loading raw v86-bridge.js inside the Terminal iframe. Create a proper terminal.html plugin using a terminal emulator UI like xterm.js, and provide placeholder assets.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal icon loads terminal.html rather than raw script
terminal.html properly instantiates the MessageChannel
Loading of Web Worker does not fail with 404

summary: Implement VFS Concurrent Write Mutex Lock
description: Prevent data collisions and file corruption by designing an asynchronous transactional Mutex (Mutual Exclusion) lock mechanism inside jsonl-storage-engine.js.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent writes to the same filePath are queued sequentially
The queue resolves in order without throwing transactional abort errors
Gzip file retains 100% data integrity under concurrent write stresses

summary: Implement CORS Proxy Bypass for Third-Party Manifest Fetching
description: Introduce a configurable CORS bypass proxy helper in index.html to allow downloading plugin manifests from remote non-CORS enabled servers.
acceptance_criteria: Dynamic App installation fetches manifests from third-party domains without triggering CORS block
The proxy path is configurable from the settings panel
Robust sanitization applies to proxy response before parsing

summary: Fix Manifest Permission Token Grammar for KB-MCP Capabilities
description: Chrome DevTools review on 2026-05-20 found that installing the bundled local manifest.json fails because plugin-installer.js rejects kb-mcp:read. The permission tokenizer currently does not allow hyphenated capability namespaces before the first colon.
acceptance_criteria: Installing http://localhost:5173/manifest.json from the Add App modal succeeds
kb-mcp:read and kb-mcp:write are accepted as valid permission tokens
Malformed or unsafe permission strings are still rejected
Regression coverage proves the bundled manifest can pass sanitization

summary: Add User-Facing KB-MCP Configuration and Health Check
description: KB-MCP runtime setup previously required window.vortexKernel.configureKb({ apiKey, kbId }) from the browser console. Settings now saves KB ID and API key presence, hides the raw saved key on reopen, and exposes a Check KB status action.
acceptance_criteria: Settings can save KB ID and API key presence without rendering the raw saved key
A health check reports configured, missing-key, missing-KB, and request-failed states clearly
A sandboxed plugin can complete a kb:read request through the host proxy after configuration
Unauthorized plugins continue to receive capability-denied errors
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed saved key is hidden after reopening Settings
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed missing and configured Settings states render clearly
Live KB success requires valid user-provided credentials

summary: Wire or Disable Placeholder Dock Apps
description: Dashboard, Files, and Terminal Dock icons now open functional windows. Repeated Dock clicks focus or restore an existing system window instead of spawning duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard and Files either open functional windows or render as visibly unavailable
Clicking every enabled Dock icon produces an observable result
The behavior is covered by a browser smoke check
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed Dashboard Dock clicks keep one window and restore minimized windows

summary: Add Favicon Asset to Remove Browser 404 Noise
description: The main route now links a small SVG favicon so browser reviews no longer confuse missing favicon noise with runtime failures.
acceptance_criteria: Loading http://localhost:5173/ no longer produces a favicon 404
Console and network reviews can distinguish real runtime issues from asset noise

summary: Fix WebContainer npm Global Install Prefix
description: Vortex OS Terminal previously let npm global installs target /usr/local/lib/node_modules inside WebContainer, causing EACCES for commands such as npm i -g @openai/codex. Global npm commands now use /home/.npm-global unless the user provides an explicit prefix.
acceptance_criteria: Global npm installs in Terminal use a writable WebContainer prefix
npm config get prefix reports /home/.npm-global
User-provided --prefix arguments are respected
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm config get prefix returns /home/.npm-global
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm i -g @openai/codex normalizes to include --prefix /home/.npm-global

summary: Remove Pyodide Vite Build Warnings
description: Terminal now loads Pyodide from the CDN module at runtime instead of statically bundling the pyodide package, removing Vite externalization warnings while preserving on-demand Python support.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal still boots Pyodide on demand
Production build completes without Pyodide externalization warnings
verification: npm run build completed successfully with no Pyodide externalization warnings

summary: Execute npm Global Binaries from Terminal Shell
description: After npm i -g @openai/codex succeeded in WebContainer, typing codex still returned codex: command not found because Vortex shell only dispatched built-in commands and did not route installed global npm binaries. Unknown safe command names now try /home/.npm-global/bin/<command> and then WebContainer PATH lookup after WebContainer has booted.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown safe command names are checked against WebContainer global npm binary paths after WebContainer has booted
Installed npm global binaries can be executed directly from Vortex shell
Non-installed commands still return a shell-level command not found
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm i -g cowsay followed by cowsay hello renders cowsay output and does not print command not found
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm i -g @openai/codex followed by codex --version executes the installed binary and does not print codex: command not found

summary: Handle Codex Native CLI Limitation in WebContainer
description: After npm i -g @openai/codex, running codex reached the installed launcher but failed with jsh: command not found: Cannot and exit code 127 because the current Codex npm package starts a native Linux ELF binary that browser WebContainer cannot execute. Vortex shell now intercepts codex and prints a clear compatibility message.
acceptance_criteria: codex no longer falls through to the WebContainer shell/native binary failure
The Terminal explains that Codex CLI must run in the host terminal or a real Linux VM, not browser WebContainer
Other npm global binaries that are WebContainer-compatible still run through the existing global binary dispatch path
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed codex prints the native-binary compatibility message
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed codex output no longer contains jsh: command not found: Cannot or Process exited with code 127

summary: Clarify Buildroot Linux VM Tooling Limits
description: The linux command boots the default v86 Buildroot image successfully, but users can reasonably try package-install commands such as curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash. The default image lacks bash and HTTPS-capable curl, producing confusing shell errors.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal help explains that the default VM is Buildroot for kernel/serial checks
Terminal points users to WebContainer/Pyodide for npm/pip workflows
Docs record that full bash/HTTPS/package-manager support needs a prepared Alpine or Debian disk image
verification: npm run build completed successfully
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed help includes the Buildroot and Alpine/Debian image requirement

summary: Add Prepared Alpine or Debian v86 Disk Image
description: Provide a real package-install Linux environment for v86 with bash, HTTPS-capable curl, CA certificates, and apk. The default Buildroot image remains suitable for kernel boot validation only.
acceptance_criteria: linux alpine boots an Alpine initramfs with bash, HTTPS-capable curl, CA certificates, and apk
The image source, build process, checksum, and size are documented
Terminal clearly distinguishes Buildroot demo mode from package workstation mode
verification: Added scripts/build-alpine-initramfs.sh to build public/v86/alpine-initramfs.cpio.gz from the official Alpine x86 minirootfs
Added scripts/resolve-alpine-apks.mjs to resolve package dependencies from Alpine APKINDEX
Added linux alpine, linux buildroot, and linux help Terminal command handling
Documented the Alpine source URL, build command, artifact size, generated SHA-256, and relay limits

Chrome DevTools MCP verified linux alpine boots Alpine 3.23.0, exposes /sbin/apk, runs GNU bash 5.3.3, runs curl 8.19.0 with https support, and receives DHCP lease 192.168.86.100 through v86 fetch relay

summary: Add WISP Relay or Same-Origin APK Mirror for Live Alpine Installs
description: The Alpine initramfs now includes bash, curl, CA certificates, apk, and v86 fetch-relay DHCP. Live apk update works through a same-origin APK mirror. Direct guest curl https://... still requires an operator-provided WISP/full TCP relay endpoint because fetch relay does not tunnel arbitrary port 443 traffic.
acceptance_criteria: linux alpine can run apk update without manual mirror/proxy setup
Guest full-TCP relay can be selected through a documented WISP relay path
Terminal docs explain how to configure or operate the relay in development and production
verification: scripts/build-alpine-initramfs.sh writes a same-origin mirror under public/v86/apk/main/x86
vite.config.js serves /v86/apk/* and /Web-OS/v86/apk/* as raw octet-stream files so .tar.gz is not decompressed by browser fetch
terminal.html rewrites /etc/apk/repositories to http://<current-port>.external/v86/apk/main after Alpine reaches the shell prompt
Chrome DevTools MCP verified apk update returns OK: 5869 distinct packages available on http://localhost:5178/Web-OS/terminal.html
linux alpine wisp://host:port and linux alpine wisps://host:port are accepted as v86 WISP relay configuration routes

summary: Operate WISP Full TCP Relay for Direct Guest HTTPS
description: The Vortex terminal can pass WISP relay URLs into v86, but this repository does not yet include an operated WISP relay daemon. Add or document an approved relay service so guest commands such as curl https://example.com work as direct outbound TCP from the VM.
acceptance_criteria: A development WISP relay endpoint is available without manual ad-hoc setup
linux alpine wisp://... or linux alpine wisps://... can run curl https://example.com successfully in Chrome DevTools MCP
Production deployment docs cover relay hosting, TLS, and security boundaries

summary: Adopt the Liquid Glass material system
description: Replace flat frosted-blur panels with a reusable Liquid Glass material (translucent tint + blur + saturate + edge highlight + inner specular highlight + soft shadow) applied to every floating surface. See docs/macos-design-guidelines.md section 2.
acceptance_criteria: A single CSS class/token set defines the Regular Liquid Glass surface and is reused by all floating surfaces
Glass surfaces use saturation 160-200% plus blur and carry edge + inner specular highlights
Light and dark tints are both defined

summary: Make the menu bar fully transparent
description: macOS Tahoe renders the menu bar fully transparent. Remove the semi-opaque slab background and blur from #menubar, keeping only legible glyphs. See section 4.
acceptance_criteria: #menubar has no background fill and no backdrop-filter
Menu-bar text stays legible over bright and dark wallpapers
Menu dropdowns remain Liquid Glass panels

summary: Introduce concentric corner-radius tokens
description: Define a radius token scale and apply it so nested rounded rectangles are concentric (child radius = parent radius minus gap). See section 3.
acceptance_criteria: All hardcoded border-radius values are replaced by radius tokens
Nested elements such as panel to row and window to toolbar button are visibly concentric

summary: Convert controls to capsule shapes
description: Buttons, segmented controls and toggles use full-capsule radii in Tahoe; text fields use the small control radius. Restyle controls, add an accent focus ring, ensure 28px+ hit targets. See section 7.
acceptance_criteria: Buttons and segmented controls render as capsules; text fields use the control radius token
Every focusable control shows an accent focus ring on keyboard focus
All interactive controls are at least 28px tall

summary: Unify the window toolbar with the window body
description: Tahoe toolbars share the window background instead of a distinct titlebar color. Remove the separate titlebar fill; give toolbar buttons only a slight drop shadow. See section 6.
acceptance_criteria: The window header no longer uses a distinct background color from the window body
Toolbar buttons remain discoverable via a subtle shadow, not a filled bar
Focused vs unfocused window states are still visually distinct

summary: Build a real Liquid Glass Control Center panel
description: The menu-bar Control Center glyph currently opens nothing. Build a Liquid Glass panel with a grid of rounded tiles so the control is functional. See section 8.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the Control Center glyph opens a Liquid Glass panel
The panel contains at least three working tiles
The panel closes on outside click or Escape

summary: Replace emoji app icons with squircle layered icons
description: Desktop and Dock apps currently use raw emoji. Render them as macOS-style squircle icon tiles with a layered background and glyph. See sections 5 and 9.
acceptance_criteria: Dock and desktop icons render as squircle tiles, not bare emoji
Icon tiles share a consistent size, radius and background treatment

summary: Honor accessibility preferences for glass and motion
description: Liquid Glass must degrade gracefully. Add media-query support for prefers-reduced-transparency, prefers-contrast and prefers-reduced-motion, and make the accent color user-selectable via the --accent variable. See sections 9 and 12.
acceptance_criteria: With reduced transparency every glass surface becomes fully opaque
With reduced motion non-essential animations are removed
The system accent color is user-selectable and applied through --accent
